name: Wadden Sea
description: The Wadden Sea is the world's largest unbroken stretch of tidal sand and mud flats, running about 500 km along the North Sea coast from the Netherlands through Germany to Denmark. Twice a day the water retreats to reveal shimmering flats, creeks and salt marshes behind a chain of low Frisian islands. Seals and porpoises live here, and huge flocks of migrating birds stop to feed.
